[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Partition Pruning and Partition Elimination in SQL Tuning"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Partition pruning and partition elimination are critical performance optimization techniques in relational database management systems (RDBMS). They allow the query optimizer to bypass scanning entire tables by targeting only the specific physical partitions that contain the relevant data."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the Core Concepts"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"When a large table is partitioned, its data is divided into smaller, more manageable pieces based on a partition key (such as a date, region, or ID). Partition pruning occurs when the database optimizer analyzes the WHERE clause of a SQL statement at compile-time (Static Pruning) or execution-time (Dynamic Pruning) and safely eliminates irrelevant partitions from the execution plan."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Static Partition Pruning: Occurs during the parsing phase when literal values are used in the filtering predicates."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Dynamic Partition Pruning: Occurs during execution, typically involving subqueries or bind variables where the exact partitions cannot be determined until the inner query resolves."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Example: Implementing and Tuning Partitioned Tables"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider a large sales table partitioned by range using the transaction date. If a query requests data for a single month, the database should only scan the partition corresponding to that month."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE sales (
    sale_id INT,
    sale_date DATE,
    amount DECIMAL(10, 2)
)
PARTITION BY RANGE (sale_date) (
    PARTITION p_2023_q1 VALUES LESS THAN ('2023-04-01'),
    PARTITION p_2023_q2 VALUES LESS THAN ('2023-07-01'),
    PARTITION p_2023_q3 VALUES LESS THAN ('2023-10-01'),
    PARTITION p_2023_q4 VALUES LESS THAN ('2024-01-01')
);"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Writing Pruning-Friendly Queries"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"To ensure the optimizer successfully leverages partition pruning, your queries must reference the partition key directly in the search conditions without wrapping it in functions or implicit data type conversions."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"SELECT SUM(amount)
FROM sales
WHERE sale_date >= '2023-05-01'
  AND sale_date < '2023-06-01';"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the query above, the optimizer evaluates the conditions against the range definitions and eliminates partitions p_2023_q1, p_2023_q3, and p_2023_q4, scanning only partition p_2023_q2."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Pitfalls Preventing Partition Elimination"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Using Functions on Partition Keys: Applying functions like EXTRACT(MONTH FROM sale_date) or TO_CHAR(sale_date, 'YYYY') disables static pruning because the optimizer cannot evaluate the function on partition boundaries."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implicit Data Type Conversions: Comparing a date partition key against a string without proper casting can prevent the optimizer from performing safe boundary checks."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"OR Conditions across Non-Key Columns: Combining predicates with OR logic where only one side references the partition key often results in a full table/partition scan."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Tuning Partitioned Workloads"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always inspect the Execution Plan (EXPLAIN PLAN) to verify that the PSTART and PSTOP operations show a restricted range instead of a full partition scan."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Align your indexing strategy with your partitioning strategy by utilizing local indexes rather than global indexes where possible."}]
